messages.content: "Can you help me calculate the energy required for a phase change? I have a science experiment where I am first melting 500 grams of ice at 0 degrees Celsius, then I am freezing it back. After that, I am vaporizing the same mass of water at 100 degrees Celsius and then condensing it back to liquid state. The substance I am using for this experiment is water. Can you tell me how much energy is required or released during each of these phase changes?"

function.name: thermo_calculate_energy
function.description: Calculate the energy required or released during a phase change using mass, the phase transition temperature and the specific latent heat. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: Mass of the substance in grams.

substance.description: The substance which is undergoing phase change, default is 'water'

message.content:
Sure!  
Below is a quick rundown of the calculations for each stage of your experiment.  

| Step | Process | Formula | Value |
|------|---------|--------|-------|
| **A** | Melt 500 g of ice → water (at 0 °C) | \(Q_{\text{melt}} = m \times L_{fus}\) | \(500\;\mathrm{g} \times 333\,\frac{\mathrm{kJ}}{\mathrm{kg}}\approx 166.7~\mathrm{kJ}\) |
| **B** | Freeze 500 g of water → ice (at 0 °C) | \(Q_{\text{freeze}} = -m \times L_{fus}\) | \(-166.7~\mathrm{kJ}\) (energy released) |
| **C** | Vaporize 500 g of water → steam (at 100 °C) | \(Q_{\text{vap}} = m \times L_{vap}\) | \(500\;\mathrm{g} \times 2256\,\frac{\mathrm{kJ}}{\mathrm{kg}}\approx 1128~\mathrm{kJ}\) |
| **D** | Condense 500 g of steam → water (at 100 °C) | \(Q_{\text{cond}} = -m \times L_{vap}\) | \(-1128~\mathrm{kJ}\) (energy released) |

### Quick notes on the numbers

| Quantity | Typical value for water |
|----------|---------------------------|
| Latent heat of fusion (\(L_{fus}\)) | \(333.55~\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{kg}\) (≈ \(333.55~\mathrm{J/g}\)) |
| Latent heat of vaporization (\(L_{vap}\)) | \(2256~\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{kg}\) (≈ \(2256~\mathrm{J/g}\)) |

> **Why the signs matter:**  
> Positive \(Q\) means energy has to be supplied (endothermic), while negative \(Q\) indicates energy is released (exothermic). In your cycle, the melt & vapourisation stages consume energy, whereas freeze & condensation release equal amounts.

If you'd like the results expressed in another unit system (e.g., calories, BTU), just let me know—happy to convert!
message.reasoning:
We need to compute energies for each step:

1) Melting 500 g of ice at 0°C -> requires latent heat of fusion (L_f). For water Lf ~ 333 kJ/kg = 334 J/g approx. Actually standard value: 333.55 kJ per kg; so per gram it's about 333.55 J/g.

So energy needed: Q_melt = m * L_f = 500g * 333.5 J/g ≈ 166750 J (~167 kJ).

2) Freezing the resulting water back into ice at 0°C releases same amount but negative sign: -Q_freeze = -166750 J (-167kJ). So energy released.

3) Vaporizing 500 g of water at 100°C: latent heat of vaporization Lv ~ 2260 kJ/kg = 2257 J/g maybe. Standard: 2256 kJ/kg. Use 2256 J/g. Energy required: Q_vap = 500*2256=1,128,000 J (~1128 kJ).

4) Condensing back releases same magnitude with opposite sign: -1,128,000 J.

Thus answer includes values. Provide explanation. Also mention units Joules or kilojoules. Possibly convert to calories if asked. But user didn't ask conversion. We'll give both J and kJ.

Also note we assume no other heating/cooling steps. Provide formula used.
